newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila money mkt lulled by expected rise in rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila money mkt lulled by expected rise in rates.

text.p: Manila's secondary market in Treasury bills saw little activity on Thursday as players stayed away expecting an increase in Treasury bill rates next week, traders said.
The renewed weakness in the Thai baht could also nudge domestic rates higher, they said.
"It (the Thai baht) will add to sentiment that rates are going to go up," a foreign bank trader said.
"Banks are cautious. They're less willing to buy bills," he added.
Traders said they were right in deciding to stay away from the market as the Central Bank later announced it was increasing its overnight borrowing rate to 15 percent from 12.75 percent.
Earlier, the Central Bank cut its overnight rates by 0.25 percentage points, pulling down the average interbank call loan rate to 12.8125 percent from 13.0625 percent.
Trades were in the range of 13 percent to 12.78125 percent, with volume at 18.47 billion pesos. Out of the 46 participating financial institutions, 25 were lenders.
